Foes of Middle-earth is fully licensed by Warner Bros. title: Resident Evil Requiem Director Has A Pretty Spicy The Legend Of Zelda Take
description: The Legend of Zelda just recently turned 40 years old, and the NES game is still cited as one of the best games of all time. But for Resident Evil Requiem director Koshi Nakanishi, it's all about arguably the black sheep in the mainline series, Zelda II: The Adventure of Link. The developer shared his love of the sequel--including its inspiration for a past Resident Evil enemy--in a new Creator's Voice video posted by Nintendo on YouTube "Of course, I played the original Legend of Zelda game, but I really loved Zelda II: The Adventure of Link game. It's more challenging, and I love it," Nakanishi said while promoting Resident Evil Requiem. The director is by no means new to the survival-horror series, previously serving in the same role for Resident Evil 7: Biohazard and Resident Evil Revelations. In fact, speaking of the latter, he shared a new anecdote about the game, which initially launched exclusively on Nintendo 3DS. "Actually, when I was making Resident Evil Revelations, there was an enemy called a Scarmiglione who carried a shield, and if you aimed at them, they would move the shield up and down. The truth is, this enemy was inspired by the armored soldier from Zelda II: The Adventure of Link," said Nakanishi. Continue Reading at GameSpot

The studio--which is owned by Sony--has also revealed rewards for Xbox gamers, which are unique for testers on the Microsoft platform. For the open beta test, Xbox Series X|S owners will receive two stylish weapon charms that can be equipped in the full game, if they decide to purchase it. While these charms don't offer any gameplay bonuses, they do look quite fashionable. The Emerald Clutch Weapon Charm and Emerald Catch Weapon Charm add some emerald flair to your weapons, and while it hasn't been confirmed, they look very Minecraft-inspired in their design. Bungie hasn't revealed the rewards for Marathon players on PC yet, but they'll likely also be a set of weapon charms. Here's a closer look at them: In comparison, PS Plus subscribers who play the Marathon beta will receive weapon charms based on Sony games like Ghost of Yotei, Death Stranding 2, and Helldivers 2. If you're interested in taking part, the Marathon Open Beta kicks off on February 26 and runs through March 2, ending just days before the full game launches on March 5. With its release date drawing closer, Bungie and Sony have begun to reveal more details on Marathon, including the soul music composed for the game and Bungie's plans to combat cheaters.
